$Comment: Names the ordinary, persistent world a player logs into 'default'. Content that should live
in the normal overworld and nowhere else targets that name instead of repeating a match
pattern in every file.
A world selector is a NAMED, REUSABLE MATCHER: 'Names' is the vocabulary this file hands out,
and 'Match'/'GameplayConfig' are the patterns a world must satisfy to earn it. Match takes the
world-name grammar Foo (exact), Foo* (prefix), *Foo (suffix), *Foo* (contains) and *
(everything); only the *Foo* form reaches a live instance world, whose name carries a random
uuid. 'ExcludeNames' drops this file's names from a world that already carries one of the
listed names, for 'everywhere except' without spelling the exceptions out as patterns.
'default' is what a fresh Hytale world is called, so the name and the pattern read the same
here on purpose - the name tells the truth about the world it points at.
IF YOUR MAIN WORLD IS NAMED SOMETHING ELSE, re-point this file rather than editing every
piece of content: drop an entry under this id in mods/ziggfreedcommon/world-selectors.json,
{ "Zc_Default": { "Names": ["default"], "Match": ["my_server_world"] } }
and everything aimed at 'default' follows. A pack can do the same by shipping its own
Zc_Default.json. To ADD worlds to the name instead of replacing the pattern, ship a file of
your own listing the same name - two files may hand out one name and both apply, because a
filename is only an address, never a meaning.
Watch out: a name nothing matches is silent. If content bound to 'default' never appears,
check your world's real name against the pattern below; the startup selector audit reports a
selector that matches none of the loaded worlds.
